topic: Understanding Fractal Dimension: Beyond Euclidean Geometry
target_audience: University students (STEM majors or curious learners)

sections.title: The Failure of Euclidean Dimensions
lecture_lines: Points, lines, and planes are Euclidean ideals.
Nature creates shapes beyond integer dimensions.
Traditional geometry fails to describe rough textures.
animations: 2. Scale segment by factor 3, observe 3 pieces (color #FF5733).

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Scaling Rule
lecture_lines: Scaling a shape by factor r increases measure.
The new measure grows by factor N.
We define dimension D using N equals r power D.
animations: 2. Scale side by 3, resulting in 9 squares [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/square.svg] (color #33FF57).
3. Show N=9, S=3 in D = log(N)/log(S).

sections.title: Defining Fractal Dimension (Hausdorff Dimension)
lecture_lines: The fractal dimension formula is log(N) over log(r).
D measures how shapes fill space efficiently.
Koch snowflakes have a dimension of 1.26.
This confirms D is not always an integer.
Fractals are infinitely complex and detailed.
animations: 1. Display Koch curve generator [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/snowflake.svg] (4 segments, color #FFFFFF).

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Fractal Lungs
lecture_lines: Lungs utilize fractal geometry for efficiency.
Branching trees maximize surface area for gas exchange.
A 2.7 dimension allows packing in the chest.
Nature optimizes space using fractal structures.
Biology thrives on complex geometric patterns.
animations: 2. Highlight increasing surface area through branching using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lungs.svg].
3. Relate complexity of [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lungs.svg] to fractal dimension > 2.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Geometry of Complexity
lecture_lines: Fractal dimension quantifies natural complexity.
It bridges the gap between chaos and order.
Everything from clouds to ferns follows this math.
Nature's roughness is measurable and beautiful.
Fractals reveal the infinite detail in existence.

2. Highlight importance of D in modeling nature.
3. Final statement on complexity beyond integers [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ferns.svg].
